name: Matthew Irwin, factor, at the government factory
head: irwin_matthew

present_on_scene_date.note: Dead or gone before 14 August 1812; in the town on the earlier dates their cards give.

associated_with.note: The United States factory outside the fort, which he kept until he left on 5 July 1812.

not_in_this_household.note: Everyone the T-3463..T-3467 day readings put in this household is on the card (liberty L-1812-town-days-3463).

persons.name: Matthew Irwin

present_on_scene_date.note: Left Chicago on 5 July 1812 (Quaife). No source takes a roll call on the afternoon of 14 August 1812; this is read from the evidence below.

persons.note: The United States factor at Chicago, who came in 1809 to keep the government factory and left on 5 July 1812. He watched the killing of Lalime. In the town from 1809-06-01 to 1812-07-05: He set out for Chicago in the spring of 1809 (Quaife ch. XIII; the arrival day is ours) and left on 5 July 1812.

evidence.quote: A short distance to the southwest were two log houses, one occupied by Matthew Irwin, the United States factor
In the spring of 1809 he again started for Chicago.
On July 5 Irwin left Chicago, having closed the storehouse and delivered the keys to Doctor Van Voorhis.

evidence.locator: Chicago Reader, 18 October 2018, the paragraph beginning 'A knife came out' (as the jaunt killing-of-jean-lalime cites it; read 2026-11-08 through a page fetch)
evidence.quote: Kinzie saw that Irwin had seen the whole thing from 20 to 30 yards away
